answerPassages.question: Does VA limit every seller-paid cost to 4%?
answerPassages.answer: VA limits seller concessions to 4% of the home's reasonable value, while ordinary closing-cost credits are separate. The VA closing-cost guidance makes that distinction. The lender must classify the actual expenses; the limit is not a promise that a seller will contribute.
answerPassages.caveat: The lender must classify the actual expenses; the limit is not a promise that a seller will contribute.

answerPassages.question: Can a temporary buydown make an unaffordable loan qualify?
answerPassages.answer: VA requires qualification using the full payment due after a temporary buydown ends. Its temporary-buydown guidance also counts seller- or builder-funded buydowns as concessions. Evaluate the later payment before accepting an early discount; a future refinance is not assured.
answerPassages.scope: VA temporary subsidy, not a permanent rate reduction
answerPassages.caveat: Evaluate the later payment before accepting an early discount; a future refinance is not assured.
